$comment: Intentional RLS classification for every application table (brief §8: CI fails if a new exposed table lacks a classification). Classifications: own_record_read | catalogue_read | server_only | public_view_backed | family_scope | tutor_scope | organisation_scope | manager_scope.

identity.users.notes: Own permanent user record; writes are server-authoritative.

identity.auth_identity_links.notes: Bridge to Supabase auth; own links only.

identity.user_preferences.notes: Last active workspace and future interface preferences; server-side writes only.

identity.user_role_assignments.notes: Workspace resolution re-checks server-side; RLS is the second layer.

permissions.role_definitions.notes: Active role catalogue readable by signed-in users.

audit.audit_events.notes: Sensitive (spec §13.4): RLS enabled, no browser policy, append-only.

families.family_accounts.notes: Readable by active members of that family only.

families.family_memberships.notes: Basis of family scope; own families only.

students.student_profiles.notes: Dependent via family link; independent via own user_id.

students.subject_section_shortlist_entri.notes: Saved shortlist; inherits subject-section scope. Cap of 3 enforced by CHECK + partial unique index.

tutors.tutor_profiles.notes: Authenticated read of publicly visible tutors only. NO anon grant — anon reads public.public_tutor_search.

tutors.tutor_verifications.notes: Labels for visible tutors; no anon grant.

services.services.notes: Published services only; no anon grant.

services.service_versions.notes: Current versions of published services; no anon grant.

platform.subjects.notes: Reference data; readable by anon and authenticated.

bookings.intended_lesson_requests.notes: Server-only: request-slice tables carry no anon/authenticated grant. Column grants are role-level and cannot distinguish a parent from a tutor, so the tutor-privacy boundary is enforced by server-side projections. RLS enabled as fail-closed second layer. The ILR is never visible to any tutor.

bookings.tutor_requests.notes: Server-only: request-slice tables carry no anon/authenticated grant. Column grants are role-level and cannot distinguish a parent from a tutor, so the tutor-privacy boundary is enforced by server-side projections. RLS enabled as fail-closed second layer. Tutor projection never selects intended_lesson_request_id, position or close_reason_code.

bookings.request_time_options.notes: Server-only, family-side. Holds the family's WHOLE set of acceptable times; the size of that set alone would tell a tutor how flexible the family is, so no tutor projection reads this table at all. RLS enabled as fail-closed second layer.

bookings.tutor_request_time_options.notes: Server-only. One tutor's own offered subset — the only option table a tutor-facing projection may read, and even there request_time_option_id is never selected because it is an identifier from the family's side. RLS enabled as fail-closed second layer.

availability.tutor_time_reservations.notes: Server-only: request-slice tables carry no anon/authenticated grant. Column grants are role-level and cannot distinguish a parent from a tutor, so the tutor-privacy boundary is enforced by server-side projections. RLS enabled as fail-closed second layer. Overlap prevented by GiST exclusion constraint.

platform.rule_settings.notes: Deadline and gate configuration is internal; never browser-readable.

availability.availability_rules.notes: Server-only: no anon/authenticated grant, no schema usage, RLS enabled with no policies (deny-all). Raw recurring availability describes when a person is and is not working. Families receive only derived positive bookable slots computed server-side by bookableSlotsForTutors.

availability.availability_exceptions.notes: Server-only, and the most sensitive table in this slice: reason_code and private_note may record a medical appointment or family circumstance. Never selected by any family-facing projection. Families receive only derived positive bookable slots, from which no gap or reason can be read.

payments.connected_accounts.notes: A tutor's Stripe Connect account and payability state. Server-only: no anon/authenticated grant and no browser policy. provider_account_id is the identifier a tutor must never see even for their own account — Studdy talks to Stripe on their behalf, and their screen shows a status, not an acct_ id. Requirement identifiers are stored so a tutor can be told what is outstanding; identity and KYC values never reach Studdy at all. Tutor-facing status is served by an explicit projection.

payments.payments.notes: Money. Server-only: no anon/authenticated grant and no browser policy. Carries provider identifiers, Studdy's commission and another family's payments, none of which any browser role may reach. Family- and tutor-facing figures are served by explicit projections, never by selecting this table.

payments.payment_events.notes: Raw provider webhook payloads and the idempotency ledger. Server-only, append-mostly; nothing here is ever family- or tutor-facing.

payments.tutor_transfers.notes: Settlement obligations to tutors. Server-only: a tutor's own earnings reach them through a projection that shows lesson price, Studdy fee and entitlement — never this table, and never Studdy's provider cost.
